theme: It exposes the hypocrites of Madinah: false oaths, fine looks, empty hearts and hostile words. Then it turns to the believers: don’t let wealth and children distract you, and spend before death comes.
story: Revealed in Madinah after the campaign against Banū al-Muṣṭaliq, in 5 or 6 AH. At a well on the way, a quarrel over water between a man of the Emigrants and a man of the Anṣār almost set the two groups fighting. The Prophet ﷺ stopped it.

ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy, leader of the hypocrites, seized the moment: “Stop spending on them and they will scatter,” and “When we return to Madinah, the more honoured will expel the more humble.” Young Zayd ibn Arqam reported it. Ibn Ubayy swore he never said it, and people blamed Zayd.
Then the surah came down, either on the journey home or just after reaching Madinah, confirming Zayd’s report. The Prophet ﷺ told him, “Allah has confirmed what you said.”

sections.title: Hypocrites claim faith behind shield oaths; impressive outside, hollow like propped wood
sections.meaning: The hypocrites testify that Muḥammad ﷺ is Allah’s Messenger. It is true, but they don’t believe it, so Allah testifies that they are liars. Their oaths are a shield. They believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed. They look impressive and speak well, yet they are hollow and fearful. Beware of them.
points: They testify you are the Messenger; Allah testifies they are liars
Oaths used as a shield, blocking people from Allah’s way
They believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed
Impressive bodies and speech, yet like propped-up wood; beware them
sections.matters: It gives the believers a clear picture of hypocrisy: saying the right words without belief, swearing to hide the truth, and looking good outside while empty inside. An enemy who hides behind friendship is the one to watch most.
sections.story: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy was about to be crowned king of Madinah when the Prophet ﷺ arrived. He became Muslim outwardly and led the hypocrites. When Zayd ibn Arqam reported his words, he swore he never said them. These ayat exposed that oath.
explained: The hypocrites come to the Prophet ﷺ and say, “We testify you are Allah’s Messenger.” The words are true, and Allah knows it, but they say them with the tongue only. So Allah testifies that they are liars. Their oaths are a junnah, a shield that protects their lives and wealth and fools people into trusting them.

They accepted faith with their tongues and rejected it in their hearts, so their hearts were sealed. Outside they look fine and speak well. Inside they are like wood propped against a wall: shapes with nothing in them. They are so afraid of being exposed that every shout in the camp seems aimed at them.
teaches: Faith lives in the heart, not only on the tongue.
Swearing a lot doesn’t make a claim true.
Don’t judge people by looks or smooth speech.
Ignoring your promise to Allah slowly hardens the heart.
A hidden enemy is more dangerous than an open one.
sections.hook: Ayah 1 says “testify” twice: they testify (nashhadu), and Allah testifies (yashhadu) that they are liars. Ayah 4 moves from how they look (ajsāmuhum) to how they sound (qawlihim).

sections.title: Proud hypocrites refuse forgiveness, threaten expulsion; treasuries and honour belong to Allah
sections.meaning: Invited to have the Prophet ﷺ ask forgiveness for them, they turn their heads away in pride. Either way, Allah won’t forgive them. They tell people to stop spending on the Prophet’s companions and boast they will expel “the humble.” But the treasuries are Allah’s, and honour belongs to Allah, His Messenger and the believers.
points: Told to seek the Prophet’s ﷺ prayer, they turn their heads away
Whether he asks forgiveness for them or not, Allah won’t forgive
“Don’t spend on them”; but Allah owns the treasuries
“The honoured will expel the humble”; honour belongs to Allah
sections.matters: It quotes the hypocrites’ own words and answers each one. They thought they controlled the believers’ food and decided who was honoured. Both claims are turned back on them: all provision is Allah’s, and real ʿizzah belongs to Allah, His Messenger and the believers.
sections.story: Ibn Ubayy said these words at al-Muraysīʿ. Once exposed, he was urged to seek the Prophet’s ﷺ prayer for forgiveness. He twisted his head away: “You told me to believe, and I did; to pay zakah, and I did. All that’s left is to bow to Muḥammad.”
explained: Told, “Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you,” they twist their heads away and turn aside in pride. They reject faith itself, so his prayer for them cannot help. Whether he asks or not, Allah will not forgive people who have left His obedience.

Then their words. “Don’t spend on those with the Messenger until they scatter,” as if the Emigrants lived off them. Yet the treasuries of the heavens and earth are Allah’s. “The more honoured will expel the more humble”: he meant himself, and the Prophet ﷺ. The truth is the reverse. Honour belongs to Allah, His Messenger and the believers.
teaches: Pride can stop a person from even asking for forgiveness.
Provision comes from Allah, not from whoever holds the money.
Real honour comes through Allah, His Messenger and faith.
Tribal pride is a call that splits believers apart.
sections.hook: Ayat 1, 4 and 5 all open with idhā (“when”). Ayat 7 and 8 each quote them, reply with wa lillāhi, and end “but the hypocrites do not understand (lā yafqahūn)… know (lā yaʿlamūn).”

sections.title: Let not wealth and children distract you; spend before death arrives
sections.meaning: Now the believers are addressed. Don’t let wealth and children distract you from remembering Allah; whoever does is a loser. Spend from what Allah gave you before death arrives and you beg for a little more time to give charity and do good. When a soul’s time comes, Allah delays no one.
points: Don’t let wealth and children distract you from Allah’s remembrance
Spend now, before death, when you beg for a short delay
No soul is delayed when its time comes
sections.matters: After exposing people ruled by love of the world, the surah turns to the believers so they don’t fall into the same trap. Wealth and children are not bad in themselves; the line is crossed when they pull you away from Allah. The chance to give ends at death.
sections.story: No specific incident. It follows the hypocrites’ story, whose schemes grew from love of worldly gain, and warns the believers against that same love.
explained: Wealth and children are the two things most likely to distract a person from dhikr, remembering Allah. Dhikr here is either the five prayers or every kind of obedience. Loving them is natural. Letting them come first makes you one of al-khāsirūn, the losers, who traded what lasts for what ends.

So spend now, while you are healthy, before the signs of death appear. Then a person begs, “My Lord, delay me a little, so I can give charity and be among the righteous”: pay the zakah and do the Hajj he put off. But when the appointed time comes, no one is delayed.
teaches: Enjoy family and wealth, but never at the cost of remembering Allah.
Give while you are healthy, not when death is near.
Don’t postpone good deeds; your time is fixed.
Regret at death cannot buy more time.
sections.hook: In ayah 7 the hypocrites say “don’t spend” (lā tunfiqū); in ayah 10 the believers are told “spend” (anfiqū). The wish “delay me” (akhkhartanī, 10) meets “Allah will never delay” (yuʾakhkhira, 11).

groups.text: The hypocrites testify he is the Messenger. Allah knows he is, and testifies that they are lying.
They hide behind oaths and block others from Allah’s way. They believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed.
They look and sound impressive, but are hollow like propped-up wood and fear every shout. They are the enemy: beware of them.
Invited to seek the Prophet’s ﷺ prayer for forgiveness, they turn away in pride. Allah will not forgive them either way.
They say “Stop spending on them” and “The honoured will expel the humble.” But the treasuries and all honour belong to Allah.
Believers: don’t let wealth and children distract you from remembering Allah, or you will be the losers.
Spend before death comes and you beg for more time. When a soul’s time arrives, Allah delays no one.

1.explain: Nashhadu: “we testify.” Their words were true, but not believed in their hearts. So Allah, who knows His Messenger is true, testifies that the hypocrites are liars in what they claim.
1.why: Revealed about ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy and his followers. Zayd ibn Arqam reported Ibn Ubayy’s words; Ibn Ubayy swore he never said them, and people blamed Zayd. The surah came down confirming Zayd.

2.explain: Junnah: a shield. Their oaths protected their lives and wealth and fooled people into trusting them. The oath is either Ibn Ubayy swearing he never said those words, or their general oaths that they are Muslims.

3.explain: They declared faith with their tongues, then rejected it in their hearts (or, in another view, truly believed and then turned back). So their hearts were sealed, and they cannot grasp faith.

4.explain: Ibn Ubayy was reportedly well-built and eloquent. Yet they are khushub musannadah: wood propped against a wall, bodies with no substance. Fearing exposure, they think every shout in the camp is about them.

5.explain: Lawwaw ruʾūsahum: they twisted their heads away, mocking and refusing. They turn from the truth in pride rather than accept the Prophet’s ﷺ prayer for them.
5.why: Reportedly revealed about Ibn Ubayy. Told to go and ask the Prophet ﷺ to seek forgiveness for him, he twisted his head away and said: “You told me to believe, and I did; to pay zakah, and I did. All that’s left is to bow to Muḥammad.”

6.explain: They are fāsiqūn: they left Allah’s obedience and chose disbelief over faith. So the Prophet’s ﷺ prayer for them cannot help, and Allah does not guide such people.

7.explain: Lā tunfiqū: they told the Anṣār to stop spending on the Emigrants so they would scatter. But all provision is in Allah’s treasuries. Thinking you feed others is folly, so: lā yafqahūn.
7.why: Ibn Ubayy told his people: “You let them settle in your land and shared your wealth. Hold back, and they will move elsewhere.” He quoted the saying, “Feed your dog until it is strong, and it will eat you.”

8.explain: Al-aʿazz, the more honoured, meant himself; al-adhall, the humble, meant the Prophet ﷺ and the Emigrants. Allah turns it around: ʿizzah belongs to Allah, His Messenger and the believers. Mistaking this is ignorance, so: lā yaʿlamūn.
8.why: Said by Ibn Ubayy after the quarrel at the well. Reportedly, his own son ʿAbdullāh, a sincere Muslim, blocked him at the edge of Madinah until the Prophet ﷺ gave him permission to enter.

9.explain: Lā tulhikum: don’t let them distract you. Dhikr Allāh is either the five daily prayers or all obedience. Whoever is distracted is among al-khāsirūn, the losers, who traded the lasting for the passing.

10.explain: Spend, including zakah, from what Allah provided, before the signs of death appear. Then a person wishes for a short delay to give charity and be righteous: to pay the zakah and do the Hajj he missed.

11.explain: When the fixed time (ajal) comes, no one gets a moment more. Allah is khabīr: fully aware of everything you do, good or bad, and He will repay it.
